intro.caption: Lesson 7-4 — comparing and ordering integers and rational numbers. Grimble has turned the Echo Hall into a game show. Tonight's boss is Rumble the stone golem, and every hit and heal goes on the board. Three rounds and a final round stand between the Delvers and the Golden Lantern.

balloons.t: Welcome to BOSS BAR SHOWDOWN! Every hit and every heal goes on the board!
Hits are negative. Heals are positive. Left on the line is LESS.
Which is bigger, −3 or −2? Easy! −3, because 3 is bigger than 2!

pages.caption: On a number line, −3 sits to the LEFT of −2. Left is less. So −3 < −2, even though 3 > 2.

balloons.t: Estimate first: which integer is it near? Then check.
I put every hit on the wall line. Farther left means less. Every time.
So the biggest hit is the LEAST number. Weird, but true.
Don't trust the digits. Trust the line.
The line and I are friends now.
FINAL ROUND! Win this, and the Golden Lantern is yours.
Champions! And Kwame only buzzed in wrong… four times.

win.caption: To compare or order numbers, picture them on the number line: farther left is less, farther right is greater. For two negative numbers, the one farther from 0 is the LESS one: −3 < −2 and −2.5 < −1.5.

gates.title: Round 1 · Estimate First
gates.prompt: Rumble's health bar shows the hits. Make an estimate before you check.
hints: Conceptual: a negative number that is farther from 0 is farther LEFT, so it is less, not greater.
Procedural: picture both numbers on a number line. Find which integers they are near. The one on the right is greater.

steps: 0.2 is a small step past −1, so −1.2 is closest to −1.

options.fb: That's the trap: thinking −3 > −2 because 3 > 2. On the line, −3 is farther left, so it is less.

options.t: −2, because it is to the right of −3

options.fb: −3 and −2 are at different points on the line. One of them is to the right.

items.label: Rumble took a hit of −3.8. Nearest integer:

fb.msg: −3.8 is almost all the way from −3 to −4. Only 0.2 more and it reaches −4.
Keep the minus sign. A hit is negative, left of 0.
That's the exact number. Estimate: which integer is it nearest?

items.fbDefault: −3.8 is between −4 and −3. Which one is it closer to?

gates.pass: Ding! −2 > −3, and −3.8 is about −4. Kwame writes "LEFT IS LESS" on his hand.

gates.title: Round 2 · Line Them Up
gates.badge: Line Master — Put Numbers in Order
gates.prompt: Sol lines up the hits and heals. Use the wall line: left is less.
hints: Conceptual: numbers increase from left to right on the number line. The least number is the one farthest left.
Procedural: place every number on the line, then read them from left to right.

steps: Practice: put 1, −5 and −1 from least to greatest.
On the line, −5 is farthest left, then −1, then 1.
worked.q: Put 4, −6 and −2 from least to greatest.

options.fb: That's the 9 > 4 trap. On the line −9 is farther left, so it is less.
−4 is to the RIGHT of −9, so −4 is the greater one.

items.q: Tap the health changes from least to greatest.
items.fb: Farther left is less. −7 is farthest left, then −3, then −2, then 0, then 2. Don't use 3 > 2 for −3 and −2.

gates.pass: −7, −3, −2, 0, 2. The wall line glows in order, and Bao's chart finally makes sense.

gates.title: Round 3 · Check on the Line
gates.badge: Line Checker — Check It on the Line
gates.prompt: Grimble says the answer. You check it with a mark on the line.
hints: Conceptual: the least number is the farthest left. Among negatives, the one farthest from 0 is the least.
Procedural: find each number on the line. Mark the one that the question asks for: farthest left for least, farthest right for greatest.

fb.msg: −1 has the smallest digit, but it is closest to 0, so it is the GREATEST of the three.
−4 is less than −1, but −6 is farther left still.

items.fbDefault: Find −6, −1 and −4. Mark the one farthest left.

fb.msg: That's the 2.5 > 1.5 trap. −2.5 is farther left, so it is less.

items.fbDefault: Find −1.5 and −2.5. Mark the one farther right.

gates.pass: Checked: −6 is the least, and −1.5 beats −2.5. Grimble grumbles into his gong.

gates.title: Final Round · The Boss Bar
gates.prompt: Three last questions. Get them all, win the Golden Lantern.
hints: Conceptual: on a number line, right is greater. For negatives, closer to 0 means greater.
Procedural: picture each number on the line before you answer. Read left to right for least to greatest, right to left for greatest to least.

steps: −0.25 is closer to 0, so it is farther right.

items.q: Lock 1 · Which symbol makes it true? −1.25 ___ −1.5

options.fb: −1.25 is to the RIGHT of −1.5, closer to 0. So −1.25 is greater.
−1.25 and −1.5 are different points on the line.

items.q: Lock 2 · Final scores: 3, −4.5, −4 and ½. Tap them from greatest to least.
items.fb: Greatest is farthest right: 3, then ½. Then −4, because −4 is right of −4.5. Last is −4.5.

items.q: Lock 3 · Kwame says −10 is the top score "because 10 is the biggest number." Judge it.

options.t: Right, 10 is bigger than the other digits
options.fb: That's the digits trap again. −10 is farthest left, so it is the LEAST score.

options.t: Wrong, −10 is the least score because it is farthest left

options.fb: −10 and 10 are opposites: the same distance from 0, but not the same value.

gates.pass: GONNNG! −1.25 > −1.5, the scores read 3, ½, −4, −4.5, and −10 is last. The Golden Lantern is yours.

journal.heading: Lesson 7-4 — what the game show taught us
rows: On a number line, numbers grow from left to right. The farther left, the less the number.
The one farther from 0 is the less one: −9 < −4 and −2.5 < −1.5.
−3.8 is about −4. Knowing where a number sits helps you check your answer.
Least to greatest: −7, −3, −2, 0, 2. Greatest to least: 3, ½, −4, −4.5.
−3 > −2 because 3 > 2 is wrong. The digits are bigger, but the number is farther left.
journal.quote: "Left is less. I wrote it on my hand. And my shield." — Kwame

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-4 (Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice.
